findings.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/logical_plan_builder.go:923` rewrites each WHERE CNF item with `asScalar=false`. In `pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:580`, `*ast.PatternInExpr` only sets `er.asScalar=true` in the `len(v.List)==1` loop default (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:602`), but for `len(v.List)!=1` it just `break`s (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:586`) leaving `er.asScalar` as false at the root. An inner IN-subquery then captures `asScalar := er.asScalar` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1175`) and only appends a scalar result when `asScalar` is true (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1297`). The outer IN-list is still lowered in `Leave` via `inToExpression` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1617`), which assumes the stack contains `lLen+1` items and unconditionally indexes `er.ctxStack[stkLen-lLen-1]` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1977`), which can go negative if the LHS produced no scalar expression.
findings.fix: In `pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:580`, when `v.Sel == nil` and `len(v.List) != 1`, set `er.asScalar = true` before `break` so the IN-list’s children (especially a nested `IN (subquery)`/`EXISTS`) are rewritten as scalar values and push an expression onto `ctxStack`. Keep the existing `len(v.List)==1` unwrap logic so the `((subquery))` case still preserves the original `asScalar` when it is truly an IN-subquery. As a hardening fallback, add a stack-length guard in `inToExpression` to return an error instead of panicking when `stkLen < lLen+1`.
findings.impact: A valid nested expression like `((TRUE NOT IN (SELECT 1)) NOT IN (0, 1))` can still trigger an out-of-bounds/panic during planning (or an internal error if recovered), which is a stability/DoS risk and breaks SQL compatibility for nested IN expressions.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`; `Enter`’s `*ast.PatternInExpr` handling still leaves the `len(v.List) != 1` path without an `er.asScalar=true` assignment, and `inToExpression` still indexes `ctxStack[stkLen-lLen-1]` without a bounds guard.
findings.verify: Add an integration test variant of the existing #63565 case with a multi-element IN list, e.g. `select 1 from tb0 where ((true not in (select 1)) not in (0,1));` (and `explain format='plan_tree' ...`). Verify it no longer panics and returns MySQL-compatible results (outer condition evaluates using the scalar value of the inner IN-subquery).
findings.what: The fix only forces scalar-context rewriting for single-element non-subquery `IN` lists. Nested `IN`-subquery expressions used as a value still break when the outer `IN` list has more than one element: the inner `IN (subquery)` is rewritten with `asScalar=false` and produces no scalar expression on `ctxStack`, but `Leave` still calls `inToExpression`, which can index `ctxStack` with a negative offset and panic.

subject: planner: fix nested IN expression rewriter bug (#63757)
summary: This commit fixes #63565’s reproduced case by forcing scalar-context rewrite when `IN` has a single non-subquery list element, so a nested `IN (subquery)` can be used as a scalar value. However, the same nested pattern still appears unsafe when the outer `IN` list has more than one element, potentially leading to a planner panic via `inToExpression` stack indexing.
